ibd_inflam_eze.name: Inflam-Eze
ibd_inflam_eze.key: 400 mg turmeric root extract, 500 mg quercetin, 200 mg ginger root extract, 2.5 g L‑glutamine
ibd_inflam_eze.src: Label: NutriDyn sell sheet 'Inflam-Eze SS ND498' Rev. 7/26 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Inflam-Eze SS ND498.pdf, opened as text with the Dropbox fetch tool 2026-11-03 and re-read 2026-11-04. Supplement Facts, serving about 1 scoop, about 14 or 30 servings per container: protein 15 g, dietary fiber 1 g, turmeric root extract 400 mg, quercetin 500 mg, ginger root extract 200 mg, L-glutamine 2.5 g, vitamin D3 10 mcg (400 IU), vitamin A 900 mcg RAE (as retinyl palmitate), vitamin C 500 mg, vitamin E 134 mg, folate 400 mcg DFE, calcium 284 mg (22% DV), iron 6.27 mg (as ferrous fumarate, 35%), magnesium 260 mg (as magnesium citrate and magnesium glycinate, 62%), zinc 13 mg (as zinc gluconate, 118%), N-acetyl-L-cysteine 200 mg, with L-lysine, cat's claw, Indian frankincense, rosemary, trans-resveratrol, milk thistle, green tea, alpha lipoic acid, broccoli sprout and devil's claw root extract (20 mg); other ingredients include calcium citrate and calcium silicate. Directions: 'Shake canister before scooping. Mix 1 scoop in 8 ounces of water twice daily or as recommended by your healthcare practitioner. Consume within 10 minutes of reconstitution. If blending, blend no longer than 15 seconds.' Caution: 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use.' The same core amounts are in products DB R266 (catalog ND143 10/1/26 as read by the Ortho Molecular and Metagenics switch charts). Name: the label, the sell sheet and the product DB all say 'Inflam-Eze' (the 'Dynamic' prefix appears only in the 5R guide and the web address), so the sheet prints 'Inflam-Eze', and GI Defend and GI Restore by their label names too. Column: the serving line is the turmeric matrix and L-glutamine; the second bullet, 'Mix in 8 oz water; drink within 10 minutes', is the label's directions ('Mix 1 scoop in 8 ounces of water', 'Consume within 10 minutes of reconstitution'), moved out of the dose bar in polish round 1 so the bar's sub-line is one line ('days 1 to 10, 2 canisters') and all five bar tops line up. Check panels: its 400 IU of D3 per scoop is counted in the 5,800 IU a day; 2 scoops give 520 mg of magnesium a day on days 1 to 10, over the 350 mg adult upper limit for magnesium from supplements (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, magnesium fact sheet; too much causes diarrhea), hence both panels' 'Looser stools on days 1 to 10?' note (its own bullet since polish round 2, so loose stools from the shake are not taken for a flare); its calcium, magnesium, zinc and iron are why both panels space ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin and doxycycline 2 hours before or 6 hours after a shake (the ciprofloxacin label's window for products with calcium, iron or zinc); its preformed vitamin A (1,800 mcg RAE a day) and the label's caution stand behind the pregnancy line; its vitamin A is all retinyl palmitate, with no beta-carotene, so the smoker line names GI Restore only. Size: R266 568 g, 14 servings (DB SKU note; R269 and the larger R266L also exist), so 10 days at 1 scoop twice daily (20 scoops) takes 2 canisters of this size, as the dose bar says. Protocol: NutriDyn 5R GI Restoration Program ND584 Rev. 1/22, REPAIR step, days 1 to 10: 'NOTE: If the patient exhibits significant GI inflammation, replace the Dynamic GI Integrity with Dynamic Inflam-Eze for improving inflammatory markers' and 'Dynamic Inflam-Eze: 1 scoop twice daily for 10 days'; Asher's Autoimmune Diseases protocol email, 2023-05-08 (lists IBD; 1 scoop in 8 oz water twice daily); NutriDyn 5R GI Restoration Program Guide, 2019 edition (Inflam-Eze is the lead product). Chosen over Inflam-Eze Plus, whose label (sell sheet ND516 Rev. 5/25) carries 200 mg white willow bark extract (25% salicin, a salicylate) and 60 mg devil's claw, which sit badly beside the front page's NSAID flare warning; Inflam-Eze has no willow bark and 20 mg devil's claw. URL: web search 2026-11-03 returns nutridyn.com/dynamic-inflam-eze (not opened: nutridyn.com is blocked from this session). PHOTO MISSING, so the column prints the gray placeholder: no Inflam-Eze powder image exists in the repo, the scratchpad, the product DB or any switch chart, and the print masters (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R266_Web, or R269_Web; 420 px web renders) cannot be downloaded from the cloud build session (Dropbox file downloads are blocked there, rechecked 2026-11-03). Stage one as build/img-src/R266.png and this entry picks it up. Never use the Inflam-Eze Plus (R856) capsule bottle instead. Photo (2026-11-04): the only reachable original is the Tropical Punch canister (R269) with the 2020 'Dynamic' label, from sell sheet ND498 Rev. 8/20; same formula family, so the size line names both flavors. Replace with the current R266 label master when it can be staged.

ibd_gi_defend.name: GI Defend
ibd_gi_defend.key: 2.5 g ImmunoLin (serum‑derived bovine immunoglobulin), from cow serum, not milk
ibd_gi_defend.src: Label: NutriDyn sell sheet 'GI Defend SS ND850' Rev. 12/24 (Dropbox Marketing Materials, opened as text 2026-11-03: Supplement Facts, serving about 1 scoop (2.5 g), about 30 servings: calories 10, protein 2 g, bovine immunoglobulin protein isolate (ImmunoLin) 2.5 g; 'Contains less than 0.05% fractionated bovine blood'; other ingredients: none; marked dairy-free; directions 'Mix 1 scoop in 8 ounces of water or your favorite beverage or as directed by your healthcare practitioner'; caution 'If pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use.' The same 2.5 g is in products DB R191 (Microbiome Labs switch chart, catalog ND143 10/1/26); size 75G (about 30 scoops, so one jar covers the 20 scoops of days 1 to 10). 'From cow serum, not milk': the label's serum-derived bovine immunoglobulin and its dairy-free mark (polish round 2: the serving line said beef serum while the column header's sub-line said cow serum; both now say cow, the plainer word for 'bovine'); also NutriDyn Nutritional Support Knowledge Base text quoted in Asher's email of 2022-05-04 (no lactose; colostrum dairy proteins are sensitizing for many). Alpha-gal: it is a mammal (beef) product, so both check panels say to skip it with a red-meat (alpha-gal) allergy, as the Joint Pain sheet does for its beef collagen (CDC, 'Products that may contain alpha-gal'). Dose: the label gives no frequency, so the protocol applies: ND584 REPAIR step 'Dynamic GI Defend: 1 scoop twice daily for 10 days'; Asher's GI-MAP protocol email, 2025-01-30, calprotectin and/or zonulin high: 1 scoop in 8 oz twice daily. 'In Inflam-Eze' (the dose bar's one-line sub-line since polish round 1): the label allows water 'or your favorite beverage'. Header (polish round 2): 'Gut immune support', the first bullet's claim and ND850's 'healthy mucosal immune system'; beside GI Restore's 'Gut lining support' the old 'Gut barrier support' read as the same need. Bullets (ND850 re-read 2026-11-04): 'Supports a healthy gut immune system' is the sell sheet's own claim, 'GI Defend helps support a healthy mucosal immune system and digestive function'; 'Supports gut barrier function' is its 'Supports healthy gut barrier function'. The earlier 'Helps bind microbial toxins in the gut' is gone (polish round 1): ND850 says ImmunoLin binds toxins that 'naturally occur in the gut during the breakdown and turnover of food', and 'microbial', beside the front page's 'Gut infections' trigger, read as an anti-infection claim. URL: products.py SLUGS (NutriDyn 60-day protocol doc) and a web search on 2026-11-03. PHOTO SOFT: build/img-src/R191.png is a 584x640 Lanczos enlargement of a 146x160 chart thumbnail (listed in img-src/soft.json), so its small label text is blurred in print. Print master: Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R191_Web, not downloadable from the cloud build session; stage it as build/img-src/R191.png and remove R191 from img-src/soft.json.

ibd_gi_restore.name: GI Restore
ibd_gi_restore.key: 2.5 g L‑glutamine, 18.75 mg zinc, 200 mg NAC, 400 mg aloe, 200 mg slippery elm, 2.5 g larch arabinogalactan
ibd_gi_restore.src: Label: NutriDyn sell sheet 'GI Restore SS ND529 NEW2' Rev. 10/26 (Dropbox Marketing Materials, opened as text 2026-11-03; the panel printed is Vanilla, serving about 1 scoop (35.78 g), 14 servings: protein 12 g, L-glutamine 2.5 g, larch arabinogalactans (FiberAid) 2.5 g, 2'-fucosyllactose 2 g, N-acetyl-L-cysteine 200 mg, zinc 18.75 mg (picolinate and zinc carnosine), quercetin 500 mg, aloe vera leaf extract 400 mg, marshmallow root 300 mg, turmeric root extract 300 mg, slippery elm bark 200 mg, vitamin D3 10 mcg (400 IU), vitamin A 7,500 mcg RAE (7,170 mcg as beta-carotene, 330 mcg as retinyl acetate), folate 185.2 mcg DFE, among others. The text layer prints names and amounts as two lists; they were paired in label order and every pair checked against its %DV. Directions: 'Shake canister before scooping. Mix 1 scoop in 8 ounces of water twice daily or as recommended by your healthcare practitioner.' Caution: 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use.' Products DB R326C (catalog ND143 10/1/26 p.101, Metagenics and Biotics Research switch charts) carries the same core amounts. Serving line (polish round 1): '2.5 g larch arabinogalactan' is the panel's own line, 'Larch Arabinogalactans (FiberAid) 2.5 g', listed last so the serving box keeps four lines (the Intestinal Permeability sheet calls it arabinogalactan); the old '2.5 g prebiotic fiber' matched no label line (the panel's Dietary Fiber line reads 2 g, and it lists three prebiotics: larch arabinogalactans 2.5 g, 2'-fucosyllactose 2 g and tapioca fiber (fiberSMART) 1.16 g). Minerals per scoop (re-read 2026-11-04, paired by %DV): calcium 254 mg (as dicalcium phosphate and calcium citrate, 20%), iron 5.7 mg (as ferrous fumarate, 32%), magnesium 35 mg (as magnesium citrate, 8%), zinc 18.75 mg (170%); with Inflam-Eze's, they are why both check panels space ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin and doxycycline from a shake. Its turmeric (300 mg) and its 400 IU of D3 per scoop are counted in the check panels (the blood-thinner line says both shakes have turmeric; 5,800 IU of D3 a day). It carries no DGL: it fills the competitor's L-glutamine + DGL + aloe slot because ND584 takes GI Integrity out of an inflamed gut (see Inflam-Eze) and GI Restore is the 5R's gut-lining shake. Size line (polish round 2): '14 servings, 2 flavors': ND529 'Servings Per Container: 14' (Vanilla panel, 'About 1 Scoop (35.78 g)', re-read with the Dropbox fetch tool 2026-11-04) and 'Available in vanilla and chocolate', so one canister lasts 7 days at 2 scoops a day. The chocolate canister's servings are not printed (541.1 g against the vanilla's 500.9 g, products DB R326C SKU notes; one chart note gives it the same 14). '14 servings, vanilla or chocolate' wraps to two lines in this column and pushes every serving box on the row down a line, so the flavors are counted, not named. Vitamin A and smokers (polish round 2): ND529 prints 'Vitamin A (as 7,170 mcg beta carotene and 330 mcg retinyl acetate) 7,500 mcg RAE' (833% DV); the parts add up to the RAE total, so the 7,170 mcg is RAE, and at 2 mcg of supplemental beta-carotene per mcg RAE (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, vitamin A and carotenoids fact sheet, after the Institute of Medicine DRIs 2001) that is about 14.3 mg of beta-carotene a scoop and 28.7 mg a day at 2 scoops (14.3 mg a day even if the 7,170 mcg were read as weight). That is the range that raised lung cancer in smokers: ATBC, 20 mg a day, lung cancer +18% in male smokers (N Engl J Med 1994, PMID 8127329); CARET, 30 mg a day with retinyl palmitate, RR 1.28 in smokers, former smokers and asbestos workers (N Engl J Med 1996, PMID 8602180); AREDS2, more lung cancers with beta-carotene, mostly in former smokers (JAMA 2013, PMID 23644932); the USPSTF recommends against beta-carotene supplements, grade D (JAMA 2022, PMID 35727271). Hence both check panels' 'Smoker or ex-smoker?' line (SMOKER in conditions/ibd.py), which asks before GI Restore only (Inflam-Eze's vitamin A is retinyl palmitate). The 660 mcg RAE a day of preformed retinyl acetate (330 mcg RAE a scoop) also stands behind the pregnancy line, with the label's caution. Protocol: ND584 RESTORE & RETAIN step 'Dynamic GI Restore: 1 scoop twice daily, from day 11 to day 24 (2 canisters)'; Asher's email of 2020-05-06: 'GI Restore ... was designed for leaky gut and Inflammatory Bowel Diseases. Is a key part of our 5R program'; NutriDyn GI Restore training deck: 'GI Restore clinical targets: ... Colitis, Crohn's'; Asher's email of 2025-01-15 on a relapsing IBD case: 'more 5R maybe for continuous months to a year', so the sheet says 'from day 11' and leaves the end to the provider. Daily rhythm: its two scoops replace the Inflam-Eze + GI Defend shake from day 11, so the plan line is written by hand (SHEET['back']['rhythm_note']: days 1 to 10, 2 pills and 4 scoops; from day 11, 2 pills and 2 scoops) and the kit's automatic count is not used. URL: web search 2026-11-03 returns nutridyn.com/dynamic-gi-restore (not opened, nutridyn.com blocked). PHOTO MISSING, so the column prints the gray placeholder: no GI Restore image exists in the repo, the scratchpad, the product DB or any switch chart; print masters Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R326V_Web and R326C_Web, 420 px, not downloadable from the cloud build session. Stage one as build/img-src/R326V.png (the Intestinal Permeability sheet's entry picks up the same file).

ibd_ultrabiotic_defense.name: UltraBiotic Defense
ibd_ultrabiotic_defense.key: 5.5 billion CFU S. boulardii, 3 billion B. lactis, 1 billion L. rhamnosus HN001
ibd_ultrabiotic_defense.src: Label: NutriDyn sell sheet 'UltraBiotic Defense SS ND458' Rev. 2/25 (Dropbox Marketing Materials, opened as text 2026-11-03: serving 1 capsule, 30 servings: Saccharomyces boulardii (Lynside) 5.5 billion CFU, Bifidobacterium lactis UABla-12 3 billion CFU, Lactobacillus rhamnosus HN001 1 billion CFU (at time of manufacture); digestive-resistant vegetarian capsule; directions 'Take one capsule daily or as directed by your healthcare practitioner'; caution 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use.' The same strains and counts are in products DB R158 (Microbiome Labs switch chart, catalog ND143 10/1/26); size 30C. The B. lactis strain code is left off the serving line for space. S. boulardii is a live yeast, so both check panels send anyone with weak immunity (many IBD medicines suppress it) or a central IV line to ask first: Enache-Angoulvant A, Hennequin C. Clin Infect Dis 2005;41:1559-68, PMID 16267727 (92 invasive Saccharomyces cases; intravascular catheters and antibiotics were the commonest predisposing factors; S. boulardii accounted for half of the fungemias), the same caution the Gut Overgrowth and Intestinal Permeability sheets print. Protocol: Asher's Autoimmune Diseases protocol email, 2023-05-08 (lists IBD; 'UltraBiotic Defense: 1 capsule daily'); NutriDyn 5R GI Restoration Program Guide, 2019 edition ('UltraBiotic Defense 1 cap 1x daily'). Bedtime: NutriDyn 60-day gut repair and detox protocol conversion doc (Drive, 2025): 'UltraBiotic Defense 1 cap At bedtime'. Antibiotic spacing: 2 hours, as in Asher's 2026 gut case study ('taken at least 2 hours away from any antimicrobial support'). URL: web search 2026-11-03 returns nutridyn.com/ultrabiotic-defense (not opened, nutridyn.com blocked). ibd_d3_5000_k2.name: D3 5000 with K2
ibd_d3_5000_k2.key: 5,000 IU vitamin D3, 60 mcg vitamin K2 (MK‑7), 15 mcg vitamin K1
ibd_d3_5000_k2.src: Label: NutriDyn sell sheet 'D3 5000 with K2 SS ND382' Rev. 6/24 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/D3 5000 with K2 SS ND382.pdf, opened as text with the Dropbox fetch tool 2026-11-03, the same label quoted in products.d/thyroid.json, pcos.json and menopause.json. Supplement Facts, serving 1 softgel, 60 servings: vitamin D3 (as cholecalciferol) 125 mcg (5,000 IU), vitamin K1 (as phytonadione) 15 mcg, vitamin K2 as MK-7 (MenaQ7) 60 mcg. Directions: 'Take one softgel daily with food or as directed by your healthcare practitioner. Do not exceed recommended dosage unless directed by your healthcare practitioner.' Warnings: 'Use should be short-term and include regular monitoring of 25-(OH)- and 1,25-(OH)2-vitamin D levels. This product contains vitamin D at a level that exceeds the adult tolerable upper intake level.' and 'Vitamin K2 may counteract the effects of anticoagulation therapy and is not recommended for patients on blood-thinning medications.' Hence the dose bar's 'check your level' (both check panels say who checks it), both editions' blood-thinner line ('Skip D3 5000 with K2'; polish round 1 cut '(its label says so)' for room) and both panels' 5,800 IU line: 5,000 IU here plus 400 IU in each of the two daily scoops of Inflam-Eze (days 1 to 10, ND498) or GI Restore (from day 11, ND529), against the adult upper limit of 4,000 IU (100 mcg; NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, vitamin D fact sheet). The same amounts are in products DB R197 (catalog ND143 10/1/26), size 60S. Protocol: ND584 REPAIR step 'D3 5000 with K2: 2 softgels per day for 10 days', then 'until bottle is finished'; Asher's Autoimmune Diseases protocol email, 2023-05-08, uses D3 10,000 with K2 (1 daily with food, higher if the level is extremely low) and says 'In autoimmune syndromes it is very beneficial to know where the vitamin D levels are'. Both protocols land near 10,000 IU a day, twice the label dose, so the sheet prints the label dose (1 softgel) and the Provider check has the provider test the level and set the dose. Other Ingredients (re-read 2026-11-04): 'Gelatin, olive oil, glycerin, purified water, calcium carbonate, turmeric extract'; the gelatin's animal is not printed. Mammalian gelatin carries alpha-gal: Mullins RJ et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2012;129:1334-42, PMID 22480538 (most patients allergic to red meat were sensitized to gelatin, and a subset was clinically allergic to both; alpha-gal was found in bovine gelatin); Wilson JM et al., Allergy 2024;79:1440-54, PMID 38193233 (alpha-gal syndrome reactions include gelatin and medications sourced from non-primate mammals). So both check panels' alpha-gal line asks before this softgel, not only before GI Defend (polish round 1). Evening meal: the label's 'with food', timed as in the NutriDyn 60-day protocol conversion doc ('D3 5000 w K2 PM'); the dose bar says 'at dinner' so its sub-line stays on one line. Product choice, OPEN FOR ASHER (asked again in polish round 2, 2026-11-04; no answer yet): the owner's notes name D3 10,000 with K2 (R172), while the sheet prints D3 5000 with K2 (R197) at 1 softgel, half the dose of both NutriDyn protocols (ND584 REPAIR: 2 softgels a day; the autoimmune protocol email: D3 10,000 with K2 daily). R197 is kept until he answers because ND584 names it, 1 softgel is its label dose (the label already exceeds the adult upper limit, and the plan stays at 5,800 IU a day instead of 10,800 IU), the check panels have the provider set the dose and how long, and its photo is a crisp 270x420 original, while R172 has only a 92x160 DB thumbnail that would print SOFT. If he picks R172: serving line '10,000 IU vitamin D3, 137 mcg vitamin K2 (MK-7), 187 mcg vitamin K1' (products DB R172, catalog ND143 10/1/26 as read by the Metagenics and Nutritional Frontiers switch charts; directions 'Take one softgel daily with food'), size 60 softgels, and restate 10,800 IU a day in both check panels. Record his answer here. URL: products.py SLUGS. Photo: build/img-src/R197.png, the 270x420 original NutriDyn web render (pooled with blasts/assets/d3-5000-with-k2.png), about 430 ppi at the 0.98 in print height; the earlier 876x1508 AI upscale was withdrawn because the upscaler rewrote label text (img-src/SOURCES.md).
